items.text: Immoi deo isolvo su filu de is fueddos e tue leadilu, giughe·lu in su mundu tuo, po chi no si ammuntonent inoghe, in su mundu meu.
items.q: You take the words with you. Does this sentence read naturally?
A film is shown this afternoon. Is 'Oe a sero' right for this afternoon?

items.text: Cheret nàrrere chi calicuna die ando a mòrrere ancora aici, de una pegariàs?
items.q: He fears dying again for no reason. Is 'de una pegariàs' clear?

items.text: – Aiat domandadu chi li facessent s'esàmene foras de turnu, pro su casu chi capitaret de aprobare.
items.q: He asked for a special exam outside the normal schedule. Is 'foras de turnu' clear?

items.text: – Càstia comente si la coghet, ti cagas su tzérebru.
items.q: Someone scolds a friend: look what a mess you made. Is that clear?

items.text: At fuidu a prus velotzidade de sa de sa lugore, si nono ja li petariat su culu.
items.q: Eskandar threatens Farid. Is it clear he'd have hung him up by the backside?

items.text: At naradu chi non la dessenhaiat pro chi restaret.
items.q: Farid writes Mozhgan's name in the dust. Is 'dessenhaiat' right for writing?

items.text: – Viiiiish, Baba, Baba, cròmpami custa pupixedda manna?
items.q: A toddler asks her dad for a big doll. Does it sound like baby talk?
